stem: Carbon forms compounds mainly by __________ electrons.
solution: Carbon shares electrons to form covalent bonds, as it has four valence electrons.

stem: The valency of carbon is __________.
solution: Carbon has four valence electrons, giving it a valency of 4 (tetravalent).

stem: A bond formed by the sharing of electrons between two atoms is called a __________ bond.
solution: A covalent bond is formed by the mutual sharing of electrons.

stem: The unique property of carbon to form long chains by bonding with itself is called __________.
solution: Catenation is carbon's ability to bond with other carbon atoms to form long chains, branches and rings.

stem: Compounds of carbon and hydrogen only are called __________.
solution: Hydrocarbons are compounds containing only carbon and hydrogen.

stem: Hydrocarbons containing only single bonds between carbon atoms are called __________.
solution: Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) contain only single carbon-carbon bonds.

stem: Hydrocarbons containing double or triple bonds are called __________.
solution: Unsaturated hydrocarbons contain carbon-carbon double bonds (alkenes) or triple bonds (alkynes).

stem: The simplest hydrocarbon, with formula CH4, is __________.
solution: Methane (CH4) is the simplest hydrocarbon (alkane).

stem: A hydrocarbon with a carbon-carbon double bond, like ethene (C2H4), is an __________.
solution: Alkenes have at least one carbon-carbon double bond, e.g., ethene.

stem: A hydrocarbon with a carbon-carbon triple bond, like ethyne (C2H2), is an __________.
solution: Alkynes have at least one carbon-carbon triple bond, e.g., ethyne (acetylene).

stem: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures are called __________.
solution: Isomers have the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements.

stem: The atom or group of atoms that determines the properties of an organic compound is the __________.
solution: A functional group determines the chemical properties of an organic compound, e.g., –OH in alcohols.

stem: The functional group present in alcohols is __________.
solution: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl (–OH) functional group.

stem: The functional group present in carboxylic acids is __________.
solution: Carboxylic acids contain the carboxyl (–COOH) functional group, e.g., acetic acid.

stem: A series of compounds with the same functional group and similar properties, differing by a –CH2 unit, is a __________ series.
solution: A homologous series has members with the same general formula and functional group, differing by CH2.

stem: Ethanol (alcohol) is commonly known as __________.
solution: Ethanol is the alcohol present in alcoholic drinks and is also used as a fuel and solvent.

stem: Acetic acid (ethanoic acid), a 5–8% solution of which is vinegar, has the functional group __________.
solution: Acetic acid (vinegar) is a carboxylic acid with the –COOH group.

stem: The complete combustion of hydrocarbons in plenty of air produces __________.
solution: Complete combustion of hydrocarbons gives carbon dioxide, water and a lot of heat (a blue flame).

stem: Incomplete combustion of a hydrocarbon (insufficient air) produces a __________ flame and soot.
solution: Incomplete combustion gives a yellow, sooty flame due to unburnt carbon particles.

stem: The addition of hydrogen to an unsaturated hydrocarbon to form a saturated one is called __________.
solution: Hydrogenation adds hydrogen across double/triple bonds, converting unsaturated to saturated compounds.

stem: Vegetable oils are converted into solid fats (vanaspati ghee) by __________.
solution: Hydrogenation of unsaturated vegetable oils converts them into semi-solid fats like vanaspati.

stem: The reaction of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol to form a sweet-smelling substance is called __________.
solution: Esterification is the reaction of an acid with an alcohol to form an ester (sweet-smelling), used in perfumes.

stem: The alkaline hydrolysis of esters (fats) to form soap is called __________.
solution: Saponification is the reaction of fats/oils with a base to form soap and glycerol.

stem: Soaps are sodium or potassium salts of long-chain __________ acids.
solution: Soaps are sodium/potassium salts of long-chain fatty (carboxylic) acids.

stem: A soap molecule cleans by having a __________ end that dissolves in water and a __________ end that dissolves in grease.
solution: Soap has a hydrophilic (water-loving) head and a hydrophobic (water-repelling) tail that dissolves grease.

stem: Soaps do not work well in hard water because they form __________ with the calcium and magnesium salts.
solution: In hard water, soap reacts with calcium/magnesium ions to form an insoluble scum, reducing cleaning.

stem: Detergents work in hard water because they __________.
options: do not form scum with calcium and magnesium ions
solution: Detergents do not form insoluble scum in hard water, so they clean effectively there.

stem: The two allotropes of carbon that are naturally hard and soft respectively are __________.
solution: Diamond is the hardest natural substance, while graphite is soft and slippery — both are allotropes of carbon.

stem: Diamond is the hardest natural substance because its carbon atoms are __________.
options: bonded in a rigid three-dimensional network
solution: In diamond, each carbon is bonded to four others in a rigid 3D network, making it extremely hard.

stem: Graphite conducts electricity and is slippery because its carbon atoms are arranged in __________.
options: layers that can slide over each other
solution: Graphite's layered structure allows layers to slide (making it slippery) and free electrons to conduct electricity.

stem: The newer allotrope of carbon shaped like a football (C60) is called __________.
solution: Fullerene (Buckminsterfullerene, C60) is a hollow, football-shaped allotrope of carbon.

stem: Which of the following is a saturated hydrocarbon?
solution: Methane has only single bonds and is saturated; ethene and ethyne are unsaturated.

stem: The addition of an alkaline potassium permanganate to an unsaturated hydrocarbon shows __________.
solution: Unsaturated compounds decolourise alkaline potassium permanganate, a common test for unsaturation.

stem: Ethanol on heating with excess concentrated sulphuric acid gives __________.
solution: Heating ethanol with concentrated sulphuric acid removes water (dehydration), forming ethene.

stem: The consumption of ethanol in large amounts is harmful because it __________.
options: affects the nervous system and health (intoxication)
solution: Ethanol is intoxicating and harmful to the nervous system and health when consumed in excess.

stem: Denatured alcohol is ethanol made unfit for drinking by adding __________.
solution: Denatured alcohol has poisonous substances added to prevent misuse for drinking.

stem: Methanol is dangerous because even small amounts can cause __________.
solution: Methanol is highly toxic; even small quantities can cause blindness or death.

stem: The general formula of the alkane homologous series is __________.
solution: Alkanes (saturated) have the general formula CnH2n+2.

stem: Carbon compounds are numerous mainly because of carbon's __________.
solution: Carbon's tetravalency and ability to catenate (form chains) allow it to form millions of compounds.

stem: Which of the following is a functional group giving a fruity smell (in esters)?
solution: The ester group (–COO–) gives compounds a pleasant, fruity smell, used in perfumes and flavourings.

stem: Which gas is produced when ethanol reacts with sodium metal?
solution: Ethanol reacts with sodium to form sodium ethoxide and release hydrogen gas.

stem: Acetic acid reacts with sodium carbonate/bicarbonate to release __________ gas.
solution: Acetic acid, being an acid, reacts with carbonates/bicarbonates to release carbon dioxide.

stem: Which of the following is an example of an unsaturated hydrocarbon?
solution: Ethene has a double bond (unsaturated); methane, propane and butane are saturated alkanes.

stem: The property of carbon that allows it to form four covalent bonds is called being __________.
solution: Carbon is tetravalent, forming four covalent bonds by sharing its four valence electrons.

stem: Soaps are effective at cleaning because they lower the __________ of water and emulsify grease.
solution: Soaps reduce water's surface tension and emulsify grease, allowing dirt to be washed away.

stem: The compound formed when acetic acid reacts with ethanol (in the presence of acid) is an __________.
solution: Esterification of acetic acid with ethanol gives an ester (ethyl acetate), which smells sweet.

stem: Coal, petroleum and natural gas are important sources of __________.
solution: Fossil fuels are rich sources of hydrocarbons and other carbon compounds.

stem: The ability of carbon to form long chains by bonding with itself is called __________.
solution: Catenation is carbon's ability to bond with other carbon atoms forming chains and rings.

stem: Compounds containing only carbon and hydrogen are called __________.
solution: Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen.

stem: The functional group in ethanoic acid (acetic acid) is __________.
solution: Ethanoic acid is a carboxylic acid with the -COOH functional group.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Carbon and its Compounds' is that:
options: carbon forms a vast number of compounds through covalent bonding, catenation and tetravalency, including hydrocarbons, alcohols, acids and useful substances like soaps and detergents
solution: The chapter explains carbon's bonding (covalent, catenation, tetravalency), hydrocarbons, functional groups, homologous series, and important compounds like ethanol, ethanoic acid, soaps and detergents.

stem: The property of carbon to form long chains, branched chains and rings of its own atoms is called __________.
solution: Catenation is carbon's ability to bond with other carbon atoms forming chains and rings.

stem: Carbon usually forms bonds by __________ electrons.
solution: Carbon shares electrons, forming covalent bonds, because it has four valence electrons.

stem: Compounds having the same molecular formula but different structures are called __________.
solution: Isomers share a molecular formula but differ in structure.

stem: Hydrocarbons containing a double or triple bond are called __________.
solution: Unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkenes and alkynes) have double or triple bonds.

stem: The general formula of alkanes is __________.
solution: Alkanes follow the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

stem: The simplest hydrocarbon, the main component of natural gas, is __________.
solution: Methane (CH₄) is the simplest hydrocarbon and the chief component of natural gas.

stem: A series of compounds with the same general formula and differing by CH₂ is called a __________.
solution: A homologous series has members differing by a CH₂ unit and similar chemical properties.

stem: The atom or group that determines the chemical properties of an organic compound is the __________.
solution: The functional group gives an organic compound its characteristic chemical properties.

stem: Ethanol on complete combustion produces carbon dioxide and __________.
solution: Complete combustion of ethanol gives carbon dioxide and water.

stem: The acid present in vinegar is __________.
solution: Vinegar is a dilute solution of ethanoic (acetic) acid.

stem: The addition of hydrogen to an unsaturated hydrocarbon in the presence of a catalyst is called __________.
solution: Hydrogenation adds hydrogen across double/triple bonds, converting unsaturated to saturated compounds.

stem: Vegetable oils are converted into vegetable ghee (vanaspati) by __________.
solution: Hydrogenation of unsaturated vegetable oils gives solid saturated fats (vanaspati).

stem: A reaction in which one atom of a hydrocarbon is replaced by another atom is a __________ reaction.
solution: Substitution reactions, typical of saturated hydrocarbons, replace one atom with another.

stem: The soap molecule has a hydrophilic (water-loving) head and a __________ tail.
solution: Soap has a hydrophilic head and a hydrophobic (oil-loving) tail.

stem: The cleansing action of soap is due to the formation of structures called __________.
solution: Soap molecules form micelles that trap oil/grease, allowing it to be washed away.

stem: Soaps do not form lather easily in __________ water.
solution: Hard water contains calcium and magnesium ions that form scum with soap, hindering lather.

stem: Detergents work better than soaps in hard water because they __________.
solution: Detergents do not form insoluble precipitates with hard-water ions, so they lather in hard water.

stem: The two allotropes of carbon that are crystalline include diamond and __________.
solution: Diamond and graphite are crystalline allotropes of carbon.

stem: Graphite is soft and used as a lubricant because its layers can __________.
solution: In graphite, layers of carbon atoms slide easily, making it soft and a good lubricant.

stem: Carbon and its compounds are used as fuels because their combustion releases __________.
options: a large amount of heat energy
solution: Combustion of carbon compounds releases large amounts of heat, making them good fuels.

stem: The number of covalent bonds a carbon atom forms is __________.
solution: Carbon forms four covalent bonds by sharing its four valence electrons.

stem: Ethanol is commonly known as __________.
solution: Ethanol is the common alcohol found in alcoholic drinks and used as a solvent and fuel.

stem: When ethanol reacts with sodium metal, the gas released is __________.
solution: Ethanol reacts with sodium to form sodium ethoxide and release hydrogen gas.

stem: Ethanoic acid reacts with an alcohol in the presence of acid to form a sweet-smelling __________.
solution: The reaction (esterification) of an acid and alcohol gives a fragrant ester.

stem: The blue flame of a gas stove indicates __________ combustion.
solution: A blue flame indicates complete combustion with sufficient oxygen.

stem: A yellow, sooty flame from a burner indicates __________ combustion.
solution: A yellow sooty flame results from incomplete combustion due to insufficient oxygen.

stem: Carbon forms a very large number of compounds mainly because of catenation and its __________ valency.
solution: Catenation and tetravalency together let carbon form millions of compounds.

stem: The bond between two carbon atoms in ethene (C₂H₄) is a __________ bond.
solution: Ethene has a carbon-carbon double bond, making it unsaturated.

stem: The bond between two carbon atoms in ethyne (C₂H₂) is a __________ bond.
solution: Ethyne (acetylene) has a carbon-carbon triple bond.

stem: Unsaturated hydrocarbons undergo __________ reactions readily.
solution: Unsaturated hydrocarbons readily undergo addition reactions across their multiple bonds.

stem: Complete combustion of hydrocarbons is preferred because incomplete combustion produces poisonous __________.
solution: Incomplete combustion forms toxic carbon monoxide, so complete combustion is safer.
